text: The Ministry of Energy said on Tuesday that the Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 95 megawatts, according to the final commissioning certificate signed by chief engineer Mara Venn and filed with the National Grid Authority. The document, dated 14 September, says the plant’s 12 turbine assemblies have been cleared for full commercial operation after a six-week performance test. Officials described the project as the first utility-scale tidal facility in the North Marches to enter service this decade. In a written statement, Energy Secretary Ivo Calder confirmed the capacity figure and said the plant is expected to supply power to about 38,000 homes annually.
